audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant, penultimate (penultimate stress), non-strict' matches both primary descriptions: Landerman 1973 (PDF p.10, verified on the page image) and Tödter et al. 2002 SLP 52 p.14, each stating regular penultimate stress with a few orthographically marked exceptions; SLP 52 p.26 identifies one systematic exception class (vocative final stress), consistent with in the dominant set/not in the strict set. Both are SIL dictionaries with orthography notes rather than phonological analyses, and no phonology article, thesis or instrumental study of Southern Pastaza Quechua was found (Glottolog has a single descriptive ref, now obtained; the 'Pastaza Quichua' prosody literature by Nuckolls is Northern Pastaza Kichwa, a different languoid), so the record rests on the best that exists: status adequate rather than well-sourced. Actions: fill the empty quote/cite/loc/grade fields from the now-held Landerman PD
